description: PRD-100 Loop 0: Design outlines for 8 research PRDs (101-108). Each story produces a structured outline with sections, key questions, research targets, and acceptance criteria that will drive Loops 1-8.

userStories.title: Design PRD-101 Outline: Mission Schema & Data Model
userStories.description: As a platform architect, I need a detailed outline for PRD-101 so that the full research PRD can be written with clear scope and structure
acceptanceCriteria: Create docs/PRDS/outlines/101-OUTLINE-MISSION-SCHEMA.md
Section 1: Problem Statement — why orchestration_runs/tasks tables don't exist yet, what gap this creates
Section 2: Prior Art Research Targets — list specific repos/systems to study: Temporal workflow schema, Prefect flow runs, Airflow DAG runs, Dagster ops, Symphony's run model
Section 3: Data Model Requirements — enumerate every entity needed: runs, tasks, events, dependencies, status enums, JSONB fields
Section 4: Key Design Questions — at least 5 questions that must be answered: DAG vs flat, event sourcing vs CRUD, state machine transitions, board_tasks integration, foreign keys to existing tables
Section 5: Existing Codebase Touchpoints — list every file/table that the schema must integrate with (board_tasks, agents, workspaces, recipes)
Section 6: Acceptance Criteria for Full PRD — what 'done' looks like for PRD-101
Section 7: Risks & Dependencies — what could go wrong, what blocks other PRDs
Outline is self-contained — someone could write PRD-101 from this outline alone
All referenced files verified to exist via grep/glob
userStories.notes: This is the foundation — every other PRD depends on the schema. Study PRD-100 Section 6 table for scope. Check existing models in orchestrator/core/models/ and alembic/versions/. The board_tasks table already exists — understand its schema before designing orchestration_tasks.

userStories.title: Design PRD-102 Outline: Coordinator Architecture
userStories.description: As a platform architect, I need a detailed outline for PRD-102 so that the coordinator service design is grounded in real research
acceptanceCriteria: Create docs/PRDS/outlines/102-OUTLINE-COORDINATOR-ARCHITECTURE.md
Section 1: Problem Statement — what coordination means in Automatos context, why heartbeat_service isn't enough
Section 2: Prior Art Research Targets — Blackboard Architecture (Nii 1986), HTN planning, BDI agents, Symphony WORKFLOW.md, CrewAI orchestration, AutoGen group chat, LangGraph state machines
Section 3: Coordinator Responsibilities — plan decomposition, agent assignment, progress monitoring, failure handling, human review gates
Section 4: Key Design Questions — LLM-driven vs rule-based planning, stateful vs stateless coordinator, how coordinator uses existing ContextService, coordinator prompt design, replanning triggers
Section 5: Integration Points — how coordinator calls AgentFactory, how it creates board tasks, how it uses tool_router, where it lives in the module hierarchy
Section 6: Acceptance Criteria for Full PRD
Section 7: Risks — coordinator complexity, LLM planning reliability, cost of coordination calls
References PRD-101 schema as dependency
All referenced Automatos files verified to exist
userStories.notes: Study heartbeat_service.py for the closest existing 'coordinator' pattern. The orchestrator_tick_llm method already does simple planning. Also read inter_agent.py for existing multi-agent coordination. PRD-100 Section 4 has the Atom→Organ hierarchy — coordinator is Organ level.

userStories.title: Design PRD-103 Outline: Verification & Quality
userStories.description: As a platform architect, I need a detailed outline for PRD-103 so that verification patterns are researched before building a critic loop
acceptanceCriteria: Create docs/PRDS/outlines/103-OUTLINE-VERIFICATION-QUALITY.md
Section 1: Problem Statement — no output validation exists today, recipes run blind, heartbeats have no quality check
Section 2: Prior Art Research Targets — LLM-as-judge (MT-Bench, Chatbot Arena), Constitutional AI critique, FutureAGI eval framework, LMSYS methodology, OpenAI evals, DeepEval, RAGAS
Section 3: Verification Taxonomy — what types of verification: factual accuracy, completeness, format compliance, success criteria matching, cross-agent consistency

Section 4: Key Design Questions — same model or different model for verification, scoring rubric design, threshold for pass/fail, human override flow, cost of verification calls, batch vs inline verification
Section 5: FutureAGI Integration — Automatos already has FutureAGI, how to leverage existing eval scanning for mission verification
Section 6: Acceptance Criteria for Full PRD
Section 7: Risks — LLM-as-judge reliability, false positives/negatives, verification cost exceeding task cost
All referenced repos/tools have URLs or references
userStories.notes: FutureAGI is already integrated — check orchestrator/core/services/ for existing eval code. The reports system (PRD-76) already has grading — study report_grade_form.tsx and the grading API. This PRD bridges existing grading with automated verification.

userStories.title: Design PRD-104 Outline: Ephemeral Agents & Model Selection
userStories.description: As a platform architect, I need a detailed outline for PRD-104 so that contractor agent lifecycle and model routing are designed with research backing
acceptanceCriteria: Create docs/PRDS/outlines/104-OUTLINE-EPHEMERAL-AGENTS-MODEL-SELECTION.md
Section 1: Problem Statement — roster agents are permanent, no mission-scoped lifecycle exists, model selection is manual
Section 2: Prior Art Research Targets — Agent Zero delegation model, Martian model routing, Unify.ai, OpenRouter model selection, AutoGen agent spawning, k8s job lifecycle
Section 3: Contractor Agent Lifecycle — spawn, configure, execute, report, destroy. What persists after destruction (reports, telemetry, board tasks)
Section 4: Model-Per-Role Strategy — which models for planning, coding, reviewing, writing. Cost vs quality tradeoffs. How OpenRouter's 340 models factor in
Section 5: Key Design Questions — DB record for contractors or ephemeral only, memory scope (mission-only vs none), tool assignment (inherit from mission or custom), spawn latency budget
Section 6: Integration with AgentFactory — how contractors use the existing agent_factory.py execute_with_prompt flow
Section 7: Acceptance Criteria for Full PRD
Section 8: Risks — spawn overhead, contractor agent quality without memory/personality, model routing accuracy
References contractor table in PRD-100 Section 3
userStories.notes: AgentFactory was just rewritten (2026-03-11) — read the clean version. It already handles tool loops and retries. Contractors need to work through the same factory. Study how heartbeat_service creates agent ticks — similar lifecycle pattern. OpenRouter is already configured in config.py with 340 models.

userStories.title: Design PRD-105 Outline: Budget & Governance
userStories.description: As a platform architect, I need a detailed outline for PRD-105 so that budget enforcement and tool policies are designed from real patterns
acceptanceCriteria: Create docs/PRDS/outlines/105-OUTLINE-BUDGET-GOVERNANCE.md
Section 1: Problem Statement — no per-mission budget enforcement, no tool policy layering, no approval gates beyond human chat

Section 2: Prior Art Research Targets — OpenClaw 6-tier tool policies, AWS billing/budgets API patterns, Kubernetes resource quotas, OpenAI usage tiers, rate limiting strategies (token bucket, sliding window)
Section 3: Budget Model — what to track: tokens, API calls, cost ($), time, tool invocations. Granularity: per-task, per-agent, per-mission, per-workspace
Section 4: Governance Layers — tool approval policies, model access policies, budget caps, human approval gates. How these compose (workspace → mission → task)

Section 5: Key Design Questions — hard cap vs soft cap, pre-estimation accuracy, what happens when budget exceeded mid-task, per-model cost tracking with OpenRouter pricing, governance config storage (DB vs YAML)
Section 6: Existing Token Budget — ContextService already has TokenBudgetManager, how to extend to mission-level
Section 7: Acceptance Criteria for Full PRD
Section 8: Risks — cost estimation inaccuracy, governance overhead, user friction from too many approval gates
userStories.notes: Read orchestrator/modules/context/budget.py — TokenBudgetManager already exists for context window budgeting. This PRD extends the concept to mission-level cost budgeting. Also check if OpenRouter returns cost info in API responses — that's the data source for tracking.

userStories.title: Design PRD-106 Outline: Outcome Telemetry & Learning Foundation
userStories.description: As a platform architect, I need a detailed outline for PRD-106 so that telemetry design enables future learning without over-engineering
acceptanceCriteria: Create docs/PRDS/outlines/106-OUTLINE-OUTCOME-TELEMETRY.md
Section 1: Problem Statement — missions will generate rich outcome data, but no structured capture exists. PRD-100 says 'raw telemetry first, learning engine later'
Section 2: Prior Art Research Targets — MLflow experiment tracking, Weights & Biases runs, Honeycomb observability, OpenTelemetry spans, A/B testing frameworks, recommendation system data models
Section 3: Telemetry Schema — what to capture per task: agent_id, model, tools_used, tokens_in, tokens_out, cost, duration_ms, verifier_score, human_accepted, error_type, retry_count
Section 4: Query Patterns — what questions the data should answer: best model for research tasks, average cost per mission type, which agents have highest acceptance rate, failure patterns by tool
Section 5: Key Design Questions — separate telemetry table vs JSONB on orchestration_tasks, retention policy, aggregation strategy, real-time vs batch analysis, privacy (what NOT to store)
Section 6: Learning Foundation — how raw telemetry enables future model routing, agent selection, and cost optimization without building those systems yet
Section 7: Acceptance Criteria for Full PRD
Section 8: Risks — data volume, query performance, storing too much vs too little, premature optimization of learning algorithms
userStories.notes: PRD-100 Section 3 explicitly says 'No fancy learning engine — just data. Query it for patterns later.' Honor this philosophy. The reports system already captures some outcome data — study the agent_reports table. Also check heartbeat_results JSONB for existing telemetry patterns.

userStories.title: Design PRD-107 Outline: Context Interface Abstraction
userStories.description: As a platform architect, I need a detailed outline for PRD-107 so that the Phase 2→3 bridge is designed with clean abstraction boundaries
acceptanceCriteria: Create docs/PRDS/outlines/107-OUTLINE-CONTEXT-INTERFACE-ABSTRACTION.md
Section 1: Problem Statement — Phase 3 swaps message-passing for shared fields, but coordinator shouldn't care which implementation is behind the interface
Section 2: Prior Art Research Targets — Hexagonal Architecture (Ports & Adapters), Clean Architecture boundary patterns, Repository Pattern for context, Strategy Pattern for field backends
Section 3: Interface Definition — what operations the coordinator needs: inject_context, query_context, subscribe_to_updates, get_relevance_score. Define abstract interface
Section 4: Phase 2 Implementation — message-passing adapter that implements the interface using existing ContextService + Redis pub/sub
Section 5: Phase 3 Implementation Preview — neural field adapter that implements same interface using shared vector space
Section 6: Key Design Questions — sync vs async interface, push vs pull context updates, granularity of context operations, how tool results flow through the interface
Section 7: Acceptance Criteria for Full PRD
Section 8: Risks — over-abstraction, interface too generic to be useful, Phase 3 requirements not yet understood well enough to design stable interface
userStories.notes: This is the critical bridge PRD. Read ContextService (service.py) carefully — it already has 8 modes and 12 sections. The interface must wrap this without breaking it. Also read the Context Engineering repo's 08_neural_fields_foundations.md for Phase 3 requirements. The interface must be narrow enough to be stable but wide enough for neural fields.

userStories.title: Design PRD-108 Outline: Memory Field Prototype
userStories.description: As a platform architect, I need a detailed outline for PRD-108 so that the neural field prototype is scoped as a concrete, testable experiment
acceptanceCriteria: Create docs/PRDS/outlines/108-OUTLINE-MEMORY-FIELD-PROTOTYPE.md
Section 1: Problem Statement — PRD-100 says 'if field prototype doesn't outperform message passing, reassess Phase 3'. This PRD defines the experiment

Section 2: Prior Art Research Targets — FAISS shared indices, Qdrant collections, Redis vector search (RediSearch), Pinecone namespaces, temporal decay in IR systems, Hebbian learning in connectionist models
Section 3: Prototype Scope — shared vector space where 2-3 agents inject findings and read amplified patterns. NOT full neural field — just enough to test the hypothesis
Section 4: Resonance Implementation — cosine similarity baseline, TF-IDF-like relevance boosting, exponential decay with reinforcement. Concrete formulas from PRD-100 Section 4
Section 5: Experiment Design — controlled comparison: same task with message-passing vs shared field. Metrics: context quality (human eval), task completion accuracy, token efficiency, latency
Section 6: Key Design Questions — vector store choice (FAISS local vs hosted), embedding model, field update frequency, decay rate calibration, what constitutes 'resonance' in practice
Section 7: Acceptance Criteria for Full PRD — must include pass/fail criteria for the experiment
Section 8: Risks — prototype too simple to be meaningful, too complex to finish, measuring the wrong thing, confirmation bias in evaluation
References Context Engineering repo sections 08-11 explicitly
userStories.notes: This is the moonshot gate. Read Context Engineering repo: 08_neural_fields_foundations.md, 09_persistence_and_resonance.md, 10_field_orchestration.md, 11_emergence_and_attractor_dynamics.md. The prototype must be simple enough to build in days, not weeks. Current memory uses Mem0 + Redis + Postgres — the prototype could layer on top. S3 Vectors is already configured (automatos-vector-index).
